chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from al-Qasim ibn al-Walid al-Amari, from Abd al-Rahman al-Asam, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah al-Amiri, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the price of the dog that does not hunt, so he said: 'It is ill-gotten gain (suh't). As for the hunting dog, there is no problem.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the price of a non-hunting dog in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the economic value of dogs based on their utility, declaring the price of a non-hunting dog as *suh't* (ill-gotten gain or worthlessness) while permitting that of a hunting dog. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that the permissibility of trade depends on the object's recognized benefit (*manfa'a*) and utility in daily life, linking the concept of *suh't* to items lacking intrinsic social or economic value.
